body: can not reproduce the issue. are you sure you are not overriding ColumnSchema::typecast() somehow?
It is already use for both ways(insert, update and default value of column) but I see the problem. need to be fixed.

I just removed the offending `\app\components\cassandra\ColumnSchema::typecast()` together with kludge `\app\components\db\ActiveRecord::__get()` and everything seems to work at first glance, incl. writes. 

But what if i'll have to resurrect it ? How can i type-hint at write and not ruin value at read ? How should i decide am i in read or write ? What is the good solution for the problem ?
there should be two methods in the framework. one for read and one for write.
something like this but we have different methods for different castings in different classes right now. have to ensure solution is clean and straight forward.

issue.body:
Table:

```
CREATE TABLE `post` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8;
```

If i do 

```
var_dump(Post::find()->one()->toArray());
```

Result: `id` is `int`

If i do 

```
var_dump(Post::find()->asArray()->one());
```

Result: `id` is `string`

Same for non-primaryKey `int` fields

body:
@samdark, @cebe 
Did the problem with read/write direction solve itself ? 

I now have to resurrect type hinting in typecast(), so have to call `debug_backtrace()` killing performance:

``` php
$isRead = in_array(debug_backtrace(false)[1]['function'],['populateRecord']);
```

I propose `typeCastRead()`, `typeCastWrite()`, and since it doesn't need separation in Yii core, just call `protected _typeCastInternal()` in `\yii\db\ColumnSchema`.
Not critical for beta release. Postponed to RC.
